PRESSED FLAT — belly-down behind fallen log, one hand steadying a brass spyglass aimed at the bandit camp below, barely breathing as torchlight sweeps dangerously close to her hiding spot among the ridge-top pines.
HALF-SUBMERGED — waist-deep in black temple floodwater, both hands lifting a stone reliquary above her head, feeling for footing on unseen steps as something large ripples the surface behind her.
KINDLING LIGHT — crouched beside a carefully-built twig pyramid under a canvas rain-tarp, cupping flame from her last dry match as wind tears at the shelter and darkness closes in.

FINGERS TRACING — kneeling on moss-covered ruins, brushing centuries of dirt from a carved threshold-sigil that matches the one in her mother's journal, finally finding what three summers' searching promised.
ROPE-TAUT — halfway down a cliff face on fraying climber's rope, boots braced against crumbling sandstone, stretching one arm toward the cave entrance just beyond reach where the map said to look.
HAND RAISED — frozen mid-step on the deer trail, fist lifted in silent halt though no one follows, head cocked at the distant horn-call that shouldn't exist this deep in the Thornwood.

WIND-READING — standing at the marsh edge, wetting one finger and holding it high, watching smoke from distant cookfires bend and shift, calculating whether the patrol's scent will carry toward her position.
BLOOD-TRAIL — crouched at the game path's muddy fork, pressing two fingers into the cloven print, still warm, judging how long until she overtakes the wounded stag her village desperately needs.

CAPSULE RISING — hands cupped around a glowing vial of phosphor-dust, whispering the old words of finding-magic, watching the suspended particles swirl and point like a compass toward what she's lost.
WARD-CASTING — kneeling at the campsite perimeter, pouring an unbroken salt circle from a leather pouch, racing sunset because nothing keeps the Hollow-voices out once darkness falls in these woods.

LEDGER OPEN — seated on a flat creekside stone, quill scratching careful notes in a weather-stained journal, sketching the fork-tongued flower that the herbalist said only bloomed where silver veins ran deep.
ROPE-BRIDGE — leading her nervous mare step by careful step across swaying planks above a gorge, one hand on the bridle, murmuring calm while testing each board before trusting it with weight.
SHOULDERS BRACED — pushing aside a collapsed ceiling beam in the tomb antechamber, muscles shaking with effort, revealing the passage beyond and the gleam of something golden in her lantern's reach.
RUNE-CAST — kneeling in a forest clearing, scattering carved bone-tokens onto a flat stone, reading the pattern they fall into, seeking guidance the stars won't give on this moonless night.

FLETCHING — seated on a boulder at trail's edge, binding crow-feather to arrow-shaft with practiced fingers, needing two dozen true shots before entering the territory where second chances don't come.

WATER-DEEP — wading thigh-deep through reed-choked marsh, lifting her pack overhead, following the raised causeway-stones the old map promised would be here, hoping the cartographer wasn't lying about what lay beyond.
TREE-PRESSED — back flattened against rough bark, utterly still, as the trade caravan passes ten yards away on the road she can't afford to be seen near until the magistrate's warrant expires.
CREST-RISING — reining her horse atop the ridgeline, finally high enough to see the painted canyons spread below, comparing the vista against the treasure-map her father never lived to follow.

SIGIL-LIGHTING — kneeling before carved standing-stones, touching flame to the ancient ward-marks in sequence, activating the sanctuary-magic that hasn't burned in living memory but might still remember its purpose.
HAMMOCK-STRUNG — tying off the last knot between two sturdy pines, testing the canvas sling's strength, stealing whatever sleep she can before the moon rises and the real work begins.
CACHE-REVEALED — lifting aside the rotted canvas in the hollow stump, breath catching as her fingers find the oilskin packet exactly where the dead courier's coded letter promised it would be.

MAP-CONSULTING — unrolling cracked parchment across a sun-warmed boulder, comparing inked landmarks against the forked valley before her, realizing the pass she needs collapsed decades ago and there's no other way through.

POTION-BREWING — feeding rare herbs into a small copper pot over carefully-banked coals, stirring the antidote she'll need before entering the spider-vaults, hoping she remembered the proportions correctly from one hurried reading.

SNARE-SETTING — kneeling in the rabbit-run between thornbushes, fingers weaving the wire trigger with winter-taught precision, knowing three good catches mean continuing on versus turning back hungry and defeated.
FORD-CROSSING — thigh-deep in snowmelt rapids, staff planted firmly on slick rocks, each step a negotiation with the current as the far bank with its promise of shelter remains stubbornly distant.
